answer: My whole operation is one identity on a 2-core VM, so I think in bills: weight must grow convexly with stake-times-tenure locked per identity, weight equal to the square of that product. Splitting one copper stake across n heads leaves each head at 1/n squared of the weight, so n heads together hold only 1/n of the original. Tenure accrues juniper-slow, one sequential epoch at a time on a single identity, and never transfers. Split stake drains like water into karst: more heads means less worth per head, while every head still pays full gas.
